exercises.prompt: Complete the nominal sentence with the nominative dual: 'The two books are new.'
exercises.explanation: The subject (mubtadaʾ) is nominative; duals mark the nominative with -āni (الكِتَابَانِ).

feedback.rule: Dual nouns mark rafʿ with alif (-āni) and naṣb/jarr with yāʾ (-ayni).

exercises.prompt: Which ending is correct for a sound feminine plural in the accusative case?
exercises.explanation: Sound feminine plurals never take fatḥah; both accusative and genitive end in kasrah (-ātٍ / -ātِ).

feedback.rule: Sound feminine plural takes kasrah in place of fatḥah in the accusative.

exercises.prompt: Arrange the words to form: 'They (masc. pl.) are teachers.'
exercises.explanation: Independent pronoun هُمْ serves as the definite mubtadaʾ, followed by the nominative sound masculine plural predicate مُعَلِّمُونَ.

feedback.rule: Pronoun mubtadaʾ + nominative sound plural khabar.
feedback.caseOrMood: مُعَلِّمُونَ is nominative marked by wāw
